title: De snackbar en de borrel
summary: Ordering at the snackbar (patatje oorlog, frikandel speciaal) and the borrel social script: rounds, bittergarnituur, proost

blocks.title: De snackbar
blocks.body: The Dutch snackbar is deep-fried, glorious and its own little language. *Patat* (fries; *friet* in the south) comes **met** (with mayo — the default) or with a dozen sauces. The classics: **patatje oorlog** ('war fries': mayo, peanut sauce and raw onion), the **frikandel** (a smooth sausage), and a **frikandel speciaal** (split open with curry ketchup, mayo and onion). Plus a **kroket** or **bitterbal** on the side.

How to order
blocks.body: Two openers do everything. **'Doe mij maar…'** (literally 'do me…' = 'I'll have…') and **'Mag ik…?'** ('may I have…?'). No need to say 'please have a nice day' first — just name it. *Doe mij maar een patatje met.* Note *met* already means 'with mayo', so you don't add the word.
blocks.callout: *Doe mij maar…* is the single most useful ordering phrase in the country.

blocks.title: De borrel
blocks.body: The **borrel** is the after-work drink that is also a whole social ritual. You gather, you order **bittergarnituur** (a shared platter of deep-fried snacks — bitterballen, cheese, mini-frikandellen), and you take turns buying **een rondje** (a round): *ik geef een rondje* = 'the round's on me'. Glasses up, look each other in the eye, and: **proost!**
blocks.callout: Skipping your round is remembered. Buying one makes you *gezellig*.
